# starblast-derived — coverage and confidence

## 1. Coverage of the closed space — the only true ratio here

The denominator is real: every constant and function the extractor found in the source, inside this epic's scope. A symbol is claimed when some use case cites it. This is the number that can carry a threshold, because it is a fraction of a finite set that was counted rather than estimated.

**Gate: ≥ 90%**

## 2. Support vector — per use case, complete or not

Five independent supports. Each is a yes or a no, so their conjunction is corroboration and not one fact counted five times. The honest target is **all five**, not 90% of them: a use case missing its acceptance criterion is not 80% testable, it is untestable.

| use case | grounded | precondition_met | postcondition_used | falsifiable | attributed | complete | sources |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---:|

## 3. The weighted rubric, and the Beta posterior

The rubric is a stated convention — grounded=40, falsifiable=25, precondition_met=12, postcondition_used=8, attributed=15 — and its number is only as meaningful as those weights, which were chosen, not measured. The posterior treats the five supports as five Bernoulli trials under a uniform prior; it is computed correctly and still rests on a prior nobody measured, which is why the 5% bound sits so far below the mean. Both are shown so the gap between them is visible.

| use case | rubric /100 | posterior mean | 5% bound | support vector |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|

## What the extractor found in the source itself

The ground space holds **28** atoms across 10 file(s). Two independent readings were taken of every constant — where it is declared, and everywhere it is read — and they disagreed in 1 place(s) with certainty:

- gem loss on damage: one source says 'gems fall off continuously as damage is taken once the shield is depleted (namu.wiki, Game Elements)', another says 'you respawn as a Tier 1 ship with minimal crystals and all upgrades vanish, which describes loss at death (fandom, How to play)' — a decision somebody has to make and record, not one a corpus should make by dropping a source
